results.proposed_proof:
**Given:** $X,f,p,\mathcal S,A$ as stated, and a closed affine embedding $X\subset\mathbb C^M$.

[F1] [[cor-dimension-of-image-plus-generic-fibre]], [[lem-classical-variety-noetherian-components]], [[lem-zero-dimensional-classical-variety-finite]] and [[lem-dimension-nonempty-open-subset]] give finite component decompositions, the generic fibre dimension formula, finiteness of zero-dimensional fibres and strict dimension drop for proper closed subsets.

[F2] [[def-finite-complex-algebraic-whitney-stratification-and-control-data]] gives the finite smooth complex algebraic Whitney strata and their incident tangent conditions. [[thm-complex-algebraic-varieties-and-maps-admit-compatible-finite-stratifications]], applied to the identity and the prescribed zero fibre, refines them to respect $f=0$ while preserving input constructibility.

[F3] [[lem-controlled-stratified-submersions-have-continuous-local-trivializations]] constructs controlled lifts and jointly continuous local flows; for proper stratified submersions its compact-trapping argument gives whole-fibre transport over compact base paths.

[F4] [[lem-complex-algebraic-stratifications-have-finite-conical-cochain-models]], Proof, step 2.2, reconstructs constructible coefficients on local products from the finite fibre cochain complexes, naturally under base-ball restriction. This is a local coefficient reconstruction assertion, not a triangulation of a real function cut. Once finite triangulations have been constructed below, [[lem-finite-simplicial-constructible-sheaves-have-a-derived-incidence-model]] gives their actual finite cochains, including deleted subcomplexes.

[F5] [[thm-generic-smoothness-characteristic-zero]] gives a nonempty target open over which a nonconstant morphism from a smooth irreducible complex stratum to the affine line is smooth; its algebraic complement has dimension zero and is finite by [F1]. A smooth locally standard presentation has surjective analytic differential in its Jacobian charts.

[F6] [[thm-heine-borel-rn]] makes closed bounded subsets of the ambient Euclidean space compact, and [[cor-bolzano-weierstrass-in-rn]] gives a convergent subsequence of each bounded sequence. Closedness keeps the limit in the chosen algebraic closed ball. For ambient dimension zero the space is a point and these conclusions hold directly.

[F7] [[lem-affine-algebraic-whitney-strata-admit-finite-critical-strongly-plurisubharmonic-distance-exhaustions]] supplies, in every prescribed nonempty real open set of centres in this same affine embedding, a squared distance with finitely many stratum critical points across all input strata.

[F8] [[lem-whitney-stratifications-admit-compatible-control-data]] supplies control data on a finite real Whitney space; [[lem-compact-semialgebraic-families-admit-compatible-finite-triangulations]] then gives finite triangulations of compact controlled Whitney spaces relative to prescribed unions of strata. Its statement does not assert arbitrary-map triangulation.

[A1] [[def-axiom-of-choice]] is inherited through [F1], [F3] and [F4]. Selecting finitely many strata and concatenating the specified transports introduces no additional choice principle.



1.1 First refine as in [F2] to respect the zero fibre. On each irreducible component of a smooth stratum where $f$ is nonconstant, [F5] gives a nonempty open of the affine line over which its differential is onto. Its proper closed complement is finite by [F1]. There are finitely many stratum components, and constant strata have one value each, so excluding the finitely many nonzero exceptional values leaves no interior stratum critical point over a sufficiently small punctured disc. [F1, F2, F5, given, construct]

2.1 For a nonconstant stratum $S$ of dimension $s$, close in $\mathbb C^M\times(\mathbb C^M)^*$ the locus $C_S^\circ=\{(x,\xi):x\in S,\ f(x)\ne0,\ df|_{T_xS}\ne0,\ \xi|_{T_xS}\in\mathbb C\,df_x\}$. Its covector fibre has dimension $M-s+1$, so every component of its closure $C_S$ has dimension $M+1$. The function $f$ is nonconstant on each base component, and its zero fibre is a proper closed subset there. Hence $\Lambda_S=C_S\cap\{f(x)=0\}$ has dimension at most $M$. The closure includes base points in lower strata; no unproved relative Thom condition is being assumed. [F1, F2, step 1.1, construct, algebra]

3.1 Identify covectors with their coefficient vectors and consider $F:\Lambda_S\times\overline{\Lambda_S}\to\mathbb C^M\times\mathbb C^M$, $F(x,\xi,y,\eta)=(x-\eta,y-\xi)$. Its source has dimension at most $2M$: applying the generic-fibre formula to the projection of each product component gives the sum of the two component dimensions. For each dominant irreducible component [F1] gives zero-dimensional, hence finite, fibres on a nonempty target Zariski open; exclude the closed image closure of each nondominant component. A common nonempty open $O$ therefore has finite fibres. The real diagonal $a\mapsto(a,\bar a)$ meets $O$ densely in every real open set: a nonzero polynomial vanishing on its proper algebraic complement remains nonzero after the invertible substitution $(a,b)=(u+iv,u-iv)$, and cannot vanish on a real open box, by induction on the number of variables using the finite-root property of each nonzero one-variable polynomial. Intersect these finitely many good parameter sets for all the strata. [F1, step 2.1, construct, algebra]

3.2 On a complex tangent space $T_xS$ where $df$ is onto, put $\ell=d|x-a|^2|_{T_xS}$. The restriction of $df$ to $\ker\ell$ fails to be onto exactly when $\ell$ is a real linear combination of $\operatorname{Re}df$ and $\operatorname{Im}df$. Indeed a real covector on the target annihilating the image of $\ker\ell$ pulls back to a multiple of $\ell$, and the converse is immediate. If the sphere is not transverse to $S$, then $\ell=0$, which is included in this obstruction. Identifying real covectors with real parts of complex covectors, the obstruction is $\bar x-\bar a\in N^*_{S,x}+\mathbb C\,df_x$. [F2, step 2.1, algebra]

4.1 The good relative-conormal centre set of step 3.1 is Euclidean open and dense. Apply [F7] within its intersection with an arbitrarily small real open neighborhood of $p$, obtaining such a centre $a$ for which the ordinary distance has only finitely many critical points on all strata. In addition to $E_a$, avoid their finitely many critical distances when choosing the radius. Thus the sphere is transverse to all strata, including those inside $f=0$. The set $E_a=\{x\in X\cap f^{-1}(0):(x,\bar x-\bar a)\in\Lambda_S\text{ for some }S\}$ is finite: every such $x$ gives $(x,\bar x-\bar a,\bar x,x-a)$ in the finite fibre of $F$ over $(a,\bar a)$. Choose $\epsilon>|a-p|$ avoiding the finitely many distances $|x-a|$ for $x\in E_a$. This choice is cofinal. Inside a prescribed $B_R(p)$ choose $|a-p|<R/4$ and $\epsilon\in(R/3,R/2)$ avoiding those distances; then $p$ lies in the ball and its closed ball lies in $B_R(p)$. [F1, F7, step 3.1, choose, construct]

5.1 If no sufficiently small punctured tube avoided that obstruction on the sphere, there would be $x_j\in S\cap\partial B_\epsilon(a)$ with $f(x_j)\ne0$, $f(x_j)\to0$ and the obstruction of step 3.2. Compactness of $X\cap\overline B_\epsilon(a)$ and finiteness of the strata give a subsequence in one $S$ converging to $x_0\in X\cap\partial B_\epsilon(a)\cap f^{-1}(0)$. Step 3.2 gives $(x_j,\bar x_j-\bar a)\in C_S$, so its limit belongs to $\Lambda_S$. Thus $x_0\in E_a$ and $|x_0-a|=\epsilon$, contradicting step 4.1. There is consequently $\delta>0$ with no sphere obstruction for $0<|f|<\sqrt2\delta$, and shrink it also as in step 1.1. [F1, F6, step 1.1, step 2.1, step 4.1, step 3.2, assume-contra, discharge-contradiction]

6.1 Over the punctured rectangle, the sphere is transverse to every input stratum and $f$ is submersive on both its interior and boundary intersections by steps 1.1, 3.2 and 5.1. Transverse intersection with a smooth hypersurface preserves Whitney conditions: the limiting tangent planes intersect its tangent kernel in the expected dimension, and the first-order Taylor formula puts limiting fibre secants in that kernel. Thus the interior/sphere intersections are a finite Whitney stratification. The closed-ball tube is proper over this base since inverse images of compact base subsets are closed in the compact $X\cap\overline B_\epsilon(a)$. The actual hypotheses of [F3] therefore hold, and its transports preserve the boundary stratum and hence the interior. [F2, F3, F6, step 1.1, step 3.2, step 5.1, construct]

7.1 On a contractible half-rectangle, fixed ordered coordinate paths and [F3]'s compact-path transports give local products and inverses. The coefficient reconstruction of [F4] transports $A$ on these products; finite interval subdivisions glue the comparisons, and reversing transport gives inverse cochain maps. These local coefficient comparisons preserve the marked boundary and therefore restrict to the open-ball interior; the global finite fibre models are constructed in the final step below. Step 4.1 supplies a cofinal family; intersecting with arbitrarily small function rectangles retains cofinality at $p$. Smooth affine charts reduce the last assertion to this construction. This proves the transport assertion. [F3, F4, step 4.1, step 6.1]


8.1 Replace the rectangle by a small circular function disc and consider $W=X\cap\overline B_\epsilon(a)\cap\{|f|\le\delta\}$. The sphere is transverse to every input stratum by step 4.1, and the function-circle boundary and its sphere intersection are transverse by step 6.1, since $df$ restricted to the sphere is onto at nonzero values. Cutting the finite Whitney strata by these transverse boundary hypersurfaces gives a compact finite real Whitney space with its outer faces unions of strata. By [F8] it has a finite triangulation respecting those faces; removing them gives a finite deleted-subcomplex model for $U=X\cap B_\epsilon(a)\cap\{|f|<\delta\}$. The compact Milnor fibre with its sphere boundary has the same finite controlled Whitney construction. Its interior therefore has a finite deleted-subcomplex model. By step 7.1 the positive-half-disc part $U_+$ is a constructible fibre bundle with that interior fibre over a contractible half-disc, giving its finite cochain model. The homology and cohomology long exact sequences for $(U,U_+)$ then give bounded finite-dimensional relative homology and cohomology. In particular these rational groups are finite free. No triangulation of the real cut $\operatorname{Re}f=0$ or of an arbitrary map has been claimed. Together with step 7.1 this proves the stated conclusions, with AC exactly through [A1]. [A1, F4, F6, F8, step 4.1, step 6.1, step 7.1] ∎

**Given:** the smooth varieties and regular functions above, rational coefficients, the indicated standard coefficients and their specified closure under operations.

[F1] [[lem-analytic-six-operation-support-and-trace-calculus]] constructs localization for arbitrary closed supports in locally compact spaces, proper base change, proper-support composition, projection and unit/counit pasting on the stated finite-dimensional domains. Temporary real half-spaces are handled in this ambient analytic category, not asserted to be complex algebraic subsets.

[F2] [[lem-analytic-constructible-sheaves-admit-coherent-six-operations]] and [[thm-verdier-duality-on-oriented-stratified-complex-varieties]] give the bounded algebraically constructible operations, proper pushforward preservation and involutive duality, with $\omega_X=\mathbb Q_X[2\dim X]$ and smooth exceptional orientation.

[F3] [[lem-algebraic-milnor-neighborhoods-admit-controlled-sector-transport]] supplies cofinal Milnor neighborhoods, their boundary-preserving controlled sector transports and the natural transport of bounded constructible coefficients.

[F4] [[lem-complex-algebraic-stratifications-have-finite-conical-cochain-models]] supplies bounded finite local and compact-support cochains and coefficient reconstruction on products. Its finite relative cochains identify localization cones and their restriction maps.

[F5] [[thm-principalization-of-ideals]] and [[prop-canonical-resolution-of-marked-ideals]] give a proper composite of smooth-centre blowups principalizing a nonzero coherent ideal on a smooth finite-type variety. Every centre lies in the controlled support. For $(f)$, the composite is consequently an isomorphism off $f=0$ and its total zero divisor has the SNC support of [[def-simple-normal-crossings-divisors]].

[F6] [[thm-holomorphic-implicit-function-theorem]] gives local roots of a nonzero holomorphic unit and the corresponding invertible SNC coordinate changes.

[F7] [[thm-alexander-whitney-and-eilenberg-zilber-are-chain-homotopy-inverses]] supplies the natural signed-shuffle and Alexander–Whitney maps and their natural prism homotopies. [[lem-relative-cohomological-kunneth-under-finite-free-homology-hypotheses]] proves the corresponding relative cohomological comparison for finite relative models over the field $\mathbb Q$; finite-dimensional rational homology is free. The supplied finite cell models and relative support cones are those of [F3]–[F4], and bounded coefficient shifts and finite totalizations preserve these comparisons.

[F8] [[thm-cover-small-inclusion-is-a-chain-homotopy-equivalence]] supplies a small-chain retraction and homotopy for an open cover, constructed with simplex-dependent least subdivision counts, preserving every subspace chain complex. [[lem-two-open-cover-small-chains-are-the-sum-of-the-two-singular-subcomplexes]] identifies cover-small chains with the sum for a two-open cover.

[A1] [[def-axiom-of-choice]] is inherited through [F1]–[F5]. The support inclusions, specified angular paths and finite coefficient calculations introduce no additional choice principle.



1.1 Put $U=X\setminus f^{-1}(0)$, let $j:U\to X$, and let $\nu:\widetilde U\to U$ be the pullback of the universal cover $\exp:\mathbb C\to\mathbb C^*$. Using bounded-below analytic injective replacements in $D^+$, before boundedness is proved, define $\Psi_fA=i^*R(j\nu)_*\nu^*j^*A$, with its unit $i^*A\to\Psi_fA$. Restrict to the lift of the positive half-plane whose logarithm has imaginary part in $(-\pi/2,\pi/2)$. This gives a natural map from $\Psi_fA$ to the restriction of the direct image from $f^{-1}\{\operatorname{Re}z>0\}$. On each cofinal Milnor neighborhood [F3], the universal cover of its punctured function rectangle and the lifted positive sector are contractible bases with the same fibre, and the coefficient reconstruction of [F4] makes this restriction a quasi-isomorphism of cochain complexes. It is therefore an isomorphism on every stalk, hence a natural sheaf isomorphism. Localization [F1] now gives $V_fA\simeq\operatorname{Cone}(i^*A\to\Psi_fA)[-1]$. In particular its stalk is the relative cochain complex of a Milnor neighborhood and its fibre; for constant coefficients this gives the displayed reduced-cohomology degree, and for $f=0$ the empty fibre gives $V_0\mathbb Q=\mathbb Q$. [F1, F3, F4, given, construct]

2.1 Expanding $\Psi$ and applying proper base change to the open and universal-cover pullback squares gives $\Psi_f Rp_*A\simeq Rp_{0*}\Psi_{fp}A$ for proper $p$. Indeed move the proper direct image past $j^*$ and $\nu^*$ by [F1], compose ordinary direct images with $R(j\nu)_*$, and move it past $i^*$ by proper base change again. This argument takes place in locally compact analytic spaces with finite-dimensional proper fibres, so it does not require constructibility to have been proved already. [F1, step 1.1, construct]

2.2 Let $P=\{\operatorname{Re}f\le0\}$, $Q=\{\operatorname{Re}g\le0\}$ and $Z=\{\operatorname{Re}(f+g)\le0\}$. On cofinal neighborhoods $U,V$ from [F3], put $A_+=U\setminus P$, $B_+=V\setminus Q$ and $L=(A_+\times V)\cup(U\times B_+)$. These are open complements, not asserted CW subcomplexes. Localization represents their support cochains by the relative complexes of $(U,A_+)$, $(V,B_+)$ and $(U\times V,L)$. The finite ordinary and Milnor-fibre models in [F3], including its compact-tube triangulation, give finite homology of $U,A_+$ and their relative pair, and similarly for $V,B_+$. No triangulation of the real cuts $P,Q$ is needed. [F1, F3, F4, step 1.1, construct]

2.3 Here is the required local duality calculation. If closed $Z_+,Z_-$ cover a locally compact space, with $L=Z_+\cap Z_-$ and inclusions $j_\pm,m$, their localization triangles give $m^*j_{+*}j_+^!A\simeq(L\to Z_-)^!j_-^*A$. To verify it, apply $j_{+*}j_+^!$ to localization for $Z_-$: the open-complement term is unchanged by support in $Z_+$ because $X\setminus Z_-\subset Z_+$, and becomes zero after restriction to $L$. Closed proper base change identifies the remaining term as stated. Dualizing these adjunction maps exchanges the two support descriptions. This calculation uses the analytic exceptional adjunction of [F1]. On the present local sector pairs, [F3] and [F4] give finite cochain and relative-cochain complexes, so dualization and evaluation are the ordinary finite-vector-space operations; no biduality theorem for arbitrary nonconstructible analytic sheaves is being invoked. [F1, F3, F4, step 1.1, construct]

3.1 To prove standard-coefficient constructibility, treat constant-function components directly and otherwise apply [F5] to $(f)$. Obtain $\pi:\widetilde X\to X$ proper, smooth upstairs, isomorphic off $f=0$, with $f\pi$ having SNC zero support. The support-centre clause in [F5] and the ordinary Rees-algebra blowup charts imply the asserted isomorphism off $f=0$ at every step. Thus $\mathbb Q_X\to R\pi_*\mathbb Q_{\widetilde X}$ is an isomorphism there, and $\Psi$, which depends only on $j^*A$, gives $\Psi_f\mathbb Q_X\simeq R\pi_{0*}\Psi_{f\pi}\mathbb Q_{\widetilde X}$ by step 2.1. This uses principalization of the function ideal, not resolution of the ambient variety alone. [F5, step 1.1, step 2.1, construct]

3.2 Here is the open-pair extension of the relative AW comparison. Write $N=C_*(A_+\times V)+C_*(U\times B_+)$ and $E=C_*(U\times V)/N$. By naturality [F7], AW, shuffle and their homotopies descend to a chain homotopy equivalence between $E$ and $C_*(U,A_+)\otimes C_*(V,B_+)$. The two indicated open sets cover $L$, so [F8] gives a small-chain retraction $R$ on $C_*(L)$ landing in $N$, with $1-R=dD+Dd$, and both $R,D$ preserve $N$. Thus $D$ contracts $J=C_*(L)/N$. Extend its contraction to a graded map $e:E\to J$ by zero on the remaining singular-simplex basis vectors. Then $T=1-de-ed$ commutes with the differential and kills $J$. It factors through a chain inverse to $q:E\to C_*(U\times V,L)$, since $qT=q$ and $T|_J=0$; its other composite is homotopic to the identity by $e$. This proves the relative chain comparison for these OPEN pairs. Subdivision depth is chosen separately for each simplex by [F8], never uniformly over all chains. [F7, F8, step 2.2, construct, algebra]

4.1 In SNC coordinates $f\pi=u(z)\prod_{i=1}^r z_i^{m_i}$ with $u\ne0$ and $m_i\ge1$. By [F6] choose a local $m_1$-st root $v$ of $u$; replacing $z_1$ by $v(z)z_1$ is an invertible coordinate change along the SNC stratum and makes the function the monomial. For small $t\ne0$ in a coordinate polydisc, put $s_i=-\log|z_i|$. The radial equation is the open convex simplex $s_i>L_i$, $\sum_i m_i s_i=-\log|t|$. The angular fibre of $\prod_i e^{im_i\theta_i}=t/|t|$ has $\gcd(m_i)$ components, each a torus $(S^1)^{r-1}$: the Euclidean algorithm extends the primitive integer row $(m_i/\gcd(m_i))$ to an invertible integer matrix, reducing its torus character to the $\gcd(m_i)$-power map in one coordinate. The tangential coordinate disc is contractible. These are finite cellular cochain models, constant in each tangential chart, and their coordinate-change transport gives locally constant finite-rank cohomology on the finitely many algebraic SNC strata. Thus $\Psi_{f\pi}\mathbb Q$ is bounded algebraically constructible. [F4, F5, F6, step 3.1, construct, algebra]

4.2 Over $\mathbb Q$, the finite-dimensional relative homology in step 2.2 is free. The algebraic part of [F7]'s relative cohomological proof applies to the free relative singular complexes with the chain comparison now proved in step 3.2: choose cycle/boundary sections, split one factor up to chain homotopy onto its homology with zero differential, and use the finite-basis evaluation inverse $w\mapsto\sum_i w(-\otimes e_i)\otimes e_i^*$. There are finitely many terms in each degree and bounded finite homology; these maps identify the actual cochain cross product with a quasi-isomorphism. Constant shifts and finite coefficient totalizations preserve it. Passing through the cofinal stalk system gives $R\Gamma_PA\boxtimes R\Gamma_QB\simeq R\Gamma_{P\times Q}(A\boxtimes B)$ for the standard inputs used here. Compose it with inclusion of supports $P\times Q\subset Z$ and restrict to the product zero fibre to define TS. This proof neither applies the CW-pair theorem to an open complement nor invokes algebraic biduality on real half-spaces. [F1, F3, F4, F7, step 2.2, step 3.2, construct, algebra]

5.1 Proper constructible preservation [F2] applied to $\pi_0$ and step 3.1 proves bounded algebraic constructibility of $\Psi_f\mathbb Q_X$, and its natural cone in step 1.1 proves the same for $V_f\mathbb Q_X$. The local relative models of [F3] and [F4] give a uniform finite bound depending on $\dim X$ for its ordinary amplitude. Standard coefficients on smooth frame charts are pullbacks by the argument below, so their unshifted amplitude equals that downstairs, independently of the auxiliary frame dimension. Constant shifts, external products and ordinary Verdier duals stay within the proved domain of [F2]; proper images do by [F2] and the comparison of step 2.1. [F2, F3, F4, step 1.1, step 3.1, step 4.1]

5.2 To prove this TS map is an isomorphism, work on a product of cofinal neighborhoods [F3], and set $\Theta=(\operatorname{Re}f,\operatorname{Re}g)$, $C=\{u\le0,v\le0\}$, $D=\{u+v\le0\}$. Localization identifies the required support comparison with restriction of complement cochains from $\Theta^{-1}(C^c)$ to $\Theta^{-1}(D^c)$. On $u>0,v<0$ deform by $H_t(u,v)=(u,(1-t)v+t\max(v,-u/2))$; on $u<0,v>0$ use the exchanged formula, and on the northeast quadrant and its positive axes use the identity. The formulas agree continuously in $C^c$, never move a coordinate through zero, do not increase absolute coordinates, send $C^c$ into $D^c$ at $t=1$, and preserve $D^c$ throughout. Thus they supply a homotopy inverse to the complement inclusion. Leave imaginary coordinates fixed and lift these paths by [F3]'s product sector transports, preserving the marked sphere boundaries and coefficients. The finite relative cochain comparisons [F4] identify restriction with a quasi-isomorphism, not merely an equality of dimensions. Cofinality and stalk detection prove that the TS map of step 4.2 is an isomorphism. [F1, F3, F4, step 4.2, construct]

5.3 For a smooth map $s:E\to X$, local product coordinates make $fs$ the pullback function and make the relative half-space pair a complex ball times the base pair. Its ordinary cochain complex is $\mathbb Q$, so [F4] gives the natural comparison $s^*V_fA\simeq V_{fs}s^*A$. It is the inverse-image map of the localization triangles and is therefore compatible with changes of product chart, composition and all support-product maps. On an affine fibration the same ordinary comparison is a homotopy-invariance isomorphism; compact-support fibre cochains are $\mathbb Q[-2e]$ for relative complex dimension $e$, with the generator integrating to $+1$. Hence the corresponding exceptional operation has the positive complex orientation and its compositional shift. [F1, F2, F4, step 1.1, step 4.2, construct]

6.1 For three functions both iterated TS maps are induced by the same inclusion $\prod_i\{\operatorname{Re}f_i\le0\}\subset\{\operatorname{Re}\sum_i f_i\le0\}$. Composition of supports and external adjunctions is associative in the actual dg localization model [F1]. Hence the maps agree under the tensor associator and obey its pentagon for every number of factors. For the zero function on a point the support inclusion and coefficient $\mathbb Q$ are identities, giving both unit laws. [F1, step 1.1, step 4.2, step 5.2]

6.2 Proper commutation of $V$ can also be seen directly: localization for $\{\operatorname{Re}f\le0\}$, proper base change for its open complement and the identity on the middle object identify its support triangle after $Rp_*$ with the support triangle downstairs. Proper restriction to $f=0$ then gives $V_fRp_*\simeq Rp_*V_{fp}$. Applying it to the ordinary unit gives $V_f\mathbb Q_X\to Rp_*V_{fp}\mathbb Q_E$. For composable proper maps the unit of the composite is the composite of units, so these coefficient maps compose. Smooth base change sends the same unit to the pulled-back unit, and the comparisons of step 5.3 identify the resulting coefficient maps. Pasting reduces to the triangle identities of [F1]. Naturality of the external-support map of step 4.2 on that unit proves compatibility with TS and external products. [F1, F2, step 4.2, step 5.3, construct]

7.1 Apply the same construction to $e^{-i\theta}f$ and $e^{-i\theta}g$. Use circular function discs inside the rectangles of [F3]; these are independent of $\theta$. The angular families of support inclusions and cochain restriction maps commute with continuation. Transport from $\theta=0$ to $2\pi$ is the positive-loop monodromy of $f+g$, and on the external product it is the simultaneous transport $T_f\otimes T_g$. TS therefore intertwines these automorphisms, without semisimplicity. This also constructs the angular comparisons used in step 1.1. [F3, F4, step 5.2, step 6.1, construct]

8.1 Apply step 2.3 to $Z_\pm=\{\pm\operatorname{Re}f\le0\}$. On $L=\{\operatorname{Re}f=0\}$ the restricted support complex is locally supported on $f=0$ near that fibre: at any other sufficiently nearby value $it\ne0$, the submersion product [F3] has zero half-space relative complex. On a closed inclusion whose intersection with a complex's support is open and closed relative to that support, ordinary and exceptional restriction agree; factor through the support and use its open restriction adjunction to verify the natural map. Thus restricting the dual calculation from $L$ to $f=0$ gives $D V_fA\simeq V_f^\pi DA$, the opposite-half-space normalization. The specified angular half-turn of step 7.1 identifies it with $V_fDA$. For the standard coefficient and its proved constructible closure [F2] applies; since $D\mathbb Q_X=\mathbb Q_X[2\dim X]$, this proves the claimed normalized duality formula. On the dual coefficient the monodromy is contragredient transport $D(T^{-1})$, making evaluation invariant; all preceding maps respect this transport by naturality. [F1, F2, F3, step 5.1, step 7.1, step 2.3]

9.1 The maps in steps 2.2–13.1 are the maps of the same support triangles, external adjunctions, orientations and specified angular transports. Their composition and proper/smooth pasting identities therefore hold simultaneously by [F1]; duality takes these identities to the corresponding identities for dual coefficients. Steps 3.1–5.1 put every standard coefficient and the stated closure in the actual constructible domain, and step 5.2 proves the load-bearing TS isomorphism. This proves all assertions, with AC exactly as in [A1]. [A1, F1, F2, step 5.1, step 5.2, step 6.1, step 7.1, step 5.3, step 6.2, step 8.1] ∎

**Given:** $Q,W$, the dimension vectors, the representation and extension stacks, and the subobject-first order.

[F1] [[def-quiver-representation-stacks-and-exact-sequence-correspondences]], [[lem-quiver-exact-sequence-correspondence-is-smooth-and-proper]] and [[lem-quiver-potential-trace-is-additive-on-extensions]] give smooth block atlases, proper invariant-flag forgetting, relative dimension $r=e-u=-\chi_Q(\mathbf b,\mathbf a)$ and equality of the restricted potential with the sum of the diagonal potentials.

[F2] [[thm-normalized-rational-vanishing-cycles-have-coherent-operations]] proves standard-coefficient constructibility, normalized duality, smooth commutation, actual coherent TS, angular monodromy and the proper coefficient map obtained from the constant-sheaf unit.

[F3] [[def-intrinsic-quotient-stack-borel-moore-grading]], [[lem-quiver-parabolic-levi-borel-model-comparisons]] and [[thm-quiver-quotient-stack-borel-moore-operation-package]] give actual induced varieties for parabolics, their Levi comparisons, the intrinsic finite-stage index and the smooth map as a vector-bundle pullback followed by inverse affine-fibration pullback. They give the flag Cartesian diagrams and positive orientations, not critical coefficients.

[F4] [[lem-product-general-linear-stiefel-approximations-stabilize-bounded-constructible-hom]] gives faithful bounded-Hom comparison for fixed bounded equivariant coefficients on sufficiently acyclic frames, with common-product and triple-product cocycles.

[F5] [[thm-constructible-six-functors-proper-base-change-and-verdier-duality]] gives normalized fixed-group duality, proper trace and the coherent ordinary operations used on those frame varieties.

[F6] [[thm-generic-smoothness-characteristic-zero]] and [[lem-zero-dimensional-classical-variety-finite]] imply that a regular function on a smooth finite-type complex variety has only finitely many critical values: outside a nonempty open of the affine line its differential is onto, and the proper closed complement is finite.
